newsitem.title: UK: Dlr exposure at record high in Feb - Merrill survey.
newsitem.headline: Dlr exposure at record high in Feb - Merrill survey.

text.p: Fund managers reporting overweight currency exposure in dollars rose sharply to a record high in February, according preliminary results from Merrill Lynch's quarterly global investor survey for February.
This heavy overweighting in dollars may well act as a lid on the dollar near-term while some of these positions are unwound and profits are taken, Merrill analysts said.

The quarterly survey, which typically polls up to 100 large international investors around the world, shows the dollar's overweight reading surged from 58 in November to 71.5 in February - its highest reading since the survey began in 1989.
A reading at 50 would indicate a net neutral positioning.

"While we believe the underlying (dollar) trend is solidly bullish, the near-term outlook is more neutral as position adjustment may dominate," said Joe Prendergast, foreign exchange strategist at Merrill Lynch in London.

Between the middle of November and the the middle of February, the dollar appreciated 14.5 percent against the German mark and 13.0 percent against the Japanese yen. --Mike Dolan, London newsroom +44 171 542 6762
